issues: The most significant resource-related issue is the lack of specific CPU core (`-n` or `-c`) and memory requests. As noted in the comments, the original SLURM script also omitted these. The script runs a long, sequential chain of shell scripts. If any of these scripts are parallel (e.g., using `make -j`), they will all compete for the limited resources of this single job allocation, which is inefficient. A better approach would be to submit them as separate jobs or as steps in a workflow.

The script is extremely non-portable. It uses hardcoded absolute paths for its working directories (e.g., `/home/projects/albany/...`). It will fail for any user not part of this project or if the directory structure changes.
The conditional `if` statement at the beginning of the script checks for `$SLURM_STEP_ID`, a variable that does not exist in a Flux environment. This part of the logic will always evaluate to false.
